CHAPTER 01 / 30ALL CHAPTERS ↑

Getting started

Your first sessionWhere to go nextWhat is saved

Your first session

  1. Create or sign in to a portal account and choose Continue game.
  2. Set your planet name, ruler name, game theme and optional music under Planet Settings.
  3. Review Mining, Population, Construction and Research. Prepare your fleet worksheet before planning an operation.
  4. Create, recover or join an alliance. The creator becomes Owner.
  5. Read Achievements and allocate claimed rewards from the Bonuses bank.

Where to go next

Use Resources & income for development, Fleet operations for missions, and Alliance recovery for saved alliance keys. A fresh or reset ticker remains stopped until manually started or newly scheduled.

What is saved

Accounts, memberships, shared intelligence and forum permissions are central. Practice simulation progress uses this browser. Keep the same browser when continuing a round; clocks shown in the header do not turn the simulation into a server ticker.

Portal, login & navigation

PortalGame menuStaff navigationFinding a rule

Portal

User control panel contains Account profile, Portal theme settings, Alliance manager, Support tickets and Create account. Staff control panel offers role-restricted tools. Portal theme settings controls the portal and manual; Planet Settings controls game appearance.

Game menu

Military groups fleet and combat systems. Foreign Affairs opens Network Hub, Galaxy Browser, Politics, Galaxy Fund, Alliance and Universe. Archive contains Satelite Uplink, Journal, Forums, Discord and Achievements. Development shortcuts open Mining, Construction, Research, Population and Planet Settings.

Staff navigation

Staff tools live in the portal. Admin Controlcenter groups Round & ticker, Planet Editor, Stats Editor, Planet tools and Havoc. Alliance Controlcenter has separate editors. Multihunters groups access logs, shared-IP review and fleet analysis. Staff can toggle the original game staff view from the portal.

Finding a rule

Choose a subject group, search for an action or use the chapter links. Search matches current chapter text. Previous and Next follow the grouped chapter order; chapter headings provide direct links.

CHAPTER 03 / 30ALL CHAPTERS ↑

Ticks, protection & saved progress

A tick advances production, population, research, construction, shipbuilding, fleet missions and temporary alliance effects. The default tick interval is one hour; the round lasts 672 ticks and has 24 ticks of protection unless changed in Admin.

The countdown follows the configured interval. Simulate tick advances a practice tick immediately. When returning after an absence, the local clock catches up in bounded steps.

Browser saves preserve the current practice round. The central database stores scan reports and sharing preferences independently. Reset replaces the browser's round; it is not a password reset or a deletion of your game account.

Normal planet attacks are blocked while protection is active. Structure planets have their own war requirement.

CHAPTER 04 / 30ALL CHAPTERS ↑

Ticker, clocks & scheduled starts

Start / restartPauseStopScheduleTime informationGame updates

Staff control panel → Admin Controlcenter → Round & ticker contains the ticker controls. A new or reset game starts with the ticker stopped and the old scheduled start cleared. Start it manually or save a new future start time. This is a browser-practice ticker: it runs while the game is open and catches up at most 24 ticks after inactivity.

▶

Start / restart

A fresh interval is scheduled. A manual action can unlock the first-start or first-restart quest once.

Ⅱ

Pause

Automatic ticks freeze and interval progress stays still. Run one tick is an explicit manual action.

■

Stop

Stops automatic ticks and resets the displayed interval bar. The first stop has a one-time quest reward.

◷

Schedule

Choose a future local date/time and save. The game must be open when processing the schedule; automatically starting never unlocks ticker quests.

Time information

The header shows current tick, next-tick countdown, an interval progress bar, a local 24-hour clock and synchronized server UTC. Page load measures browser navigation time; Server RTT measures the full network round trip. These clocks do not mean the simulation runs as a server-authoritative ticker.

Game updates

Starts, pauses and stops confirm with a toast and prominent yellow/black entries in Recent signals and News Log. Toggle the Game updates category in the news filters.

CHAPTER 06 / 30ALL CHAPTERS ↑

Resources, asteroids & income

Income calculationMining capacity

Metal, Crystal and Eonium pay for development, ship production, scans and self exile. Each resource has an asteroid field, a refinery and a resource reserve.

Income calculation

Core Mining levels 0–4 provide respectively 1,000; 3,500; 7,000; 12,500; 20,000 base income for each resource. Every asteroid adds 250 per tick, and every matching refinery adds 1,100.

The base amount is multiplied by mining workforce and finance bonuses, the round income multiplier and applicable alliance effects. Each Finance Centre adds 0.5%. Your displayed resource rate reflects these factors and any enabled alliance tax.

Mining capacity

Heavy Cargo Transfers increases asteroid capacity. The progression is 100, 200, 300, 500, 750, 1,000, 1,250, 1,500, 2,000, 2,500, 3,000, 3,500, 4,500, 5,500, 6,500, 8,000 and 10,000 asteroids.

Planet value includes holdings such as resources, ships, buildings and asteroids; the practice score adds earned experience to that value. The game shows its current calculation in the planet and galaxy views.

Nationalism−10%0%

Apply to running ship orders

Population → Shipwrights supplies the population percentage bonus. Output uses the additive factor 1 + (population bonus + government bonus) / 100. Starfall retains its existing factory build-point base and round multiplier; this update implements the manual’s production bonuses, not the entire Planetarion production-unit economy. Factory allocation remains attached to each numbered order.

Population and government output changes update the current order’s ETA and the next tick’s work immediately, without resetting progress or changing its paid costs. Government cost discounts apply only when placing a new order and are shown in the price preview. Cancellation refunds half of the cost actually paid.

Government selection

Choose a government under Population. First formation within the first 168 ticks is free. A later formation or a change starts a 72-tick revolution, using the Anarchy production penalty. Government mining, research and construction modifiers also apply to the current practice base rates. Covert ops separately uses the stealth and alert modifiers.

CHAPTER 08 / 30ALL CHAPTERS ↑

Population & workforce

The five workforce assignments are Mining, Research, Construction, Shipwright and Security. The assignments must total exactly 100% before they can be applied.

Mining improves resource output. Research staffing scales research points; Construction scales construction units; Shipwright staffing scales factory production. Security is a dedicated allocation in the practice workforce model.

Population increases on ticks. The default practice allocation is 40% Mining, 20% Research, 20% Construction, 15% Shipwright and 5% Security. Change the allocation as your immediate needs change, then press Assign workforce.

Buildings & construction

Construction spends resources and progresses through construction units. One active order can be accompanied by queued orders. The game shows the remaining work and estimated ticks; cancel controls describe the refund available for that order.

Construction output is based on staffing: a 20% construction allocation provides 100 construction units per tick. Building costs and capacity may change with development, so the order card is the authoritative price before purchase.

Draft orders: ships & asteroids

Choose an amountAdd to orderOrder allDeliveryIndependent orders

Ship Production and Mining share the same two-stage ordering workflow. Drafts persist in the browser and do not charge resources.

01

Choose an amount

Enter the number of ships or asteroids. For ships, choose Base or Fleet 1–3 as the delivery destination.

02

Add to order

Build a draft from several ship types or resource types. Remove entries or clear the draft before confirming.

03

Order all

The whole bill is checked against resources, research and capacity. Failure preserves the draft without partial payment.

04

Delivery

Ships arrive in their selected fleet on completion. Asteroids are initiated immediately using their current rising prices.

Independent orders

Order now remains available on every card. Ship orders still use one active and one queued order; asteroid orders retain mining capacity limits.

Each supported quest shows its lore, exact reward and progress before completion. A completion medal marks a reached goal; claiming upgrades it to gold. Every quest is claimable once per round. A one-time startup grant supplies 2,000,000 of each resource. Its RP/CU totals depend on the race at import. No previous-round loyalty bonus is invented.

CHAPTER 13 / 30ALL CHAPTERS ↑

Factories, ship production & fleets

Fleet managementShip roster

Production lists the ships for your planet's race. An order requires the matching hull research, the correct factory and enough resources. Enter a quantity to see the total cost before ordering.

Light factories build Fighters and Corvettes. Medium factories serve Frigates, Destroyers and Cruisers; Heavy factories build Battleships. Assign owned factories to production to make use of their throughput. Queue and cancel controls manage ongoing orders.

Autofill buttons calculate the ships needed to reach a target fleet total, rather than ordering that many additional ships.

Fleet management

Your ships occupy Base, personal Fleet 1–3 and the permanent fourth Alliance Fleet. Transfer ships into a field fleet before launching a mission. Launching removes those ships from the ready fleet and creates an outbound mission. Recall controls send active missions home.

Out-of-galaxy travel starts at 12 ticks for Fighters and Corvettes, plus one for Frigates and Destroyers or two for Cruisers and Battleships. Space Travel removes up to four ticks. Same-alliance defence removes one more; in-galaxy defence takes five ticks. The practice Transwarp Hub can reduce out-of-galaxy travel by one.

Ship roster

Every race has a distinct roster and artwork. Production cards expose targeting, initiative, guns, damage, armour, role, cloak, ETA and cost. Use those current cards and the battle calculator when composing a fleet.

CHAPTER 14 / 30ALL CHAPTERS ↑

Fleet operations & vendor sales

Themes & calculatorNetwork HubPersonalised fleetsScheduled launchesFake DefenceShip AnalysisVendor sales

Themes & calculator

Classic is an old-school in-game skin under Planet Settings. Nyan Cat is a portal/manual arcade theme under User Control Panel and joins theme cycling. Fleets → Add to Calc loads the selected ready and deployed fleet as attacker, preserves defender inputs and opens the battle calculator.

Network Hub

Network Hub replaces Galaxy Status. Incoming, outgoing and returning fleets are separate tables. Enable alliance intel adds permitted alliance threat reports and assessments. Unknown counts and origins remain unknown.

Personalised fleets

Fleets → Personalised fleet names accepts three distinct names of 3–15 letters or numbers. Internal fleet slots remain unchanged.

Scheduled launches

Set a delay of 0–12 ticks before launching. Ships are reserved immediately and depart when the practice ticker reaches that tick. Cancelling before departure returns them immediately. This browser practice ticker must be running or catch up for the schedule to execute.

Fake Defence

Fake Defence recalls automatically when travel reaches ETA 1, before arrival. It returns over the travelled distance.

Ship Analysis

The table totals normal damage, EMP shots and stealing damage against primary target classes across ready and deployed ships. Enemy resistance, initiative and target priority affect actual combat; use the battle calculator for a battle estimate.

Vendor sales

Production → Sell ships removes ships from the Base fleet for 12 ticks. The practice vendor pays a displayed fixed 50% of catalog resource cost; this rate is a Starfall rule. Cancelling returns the ships after a new 12-tick trip. Ships with the vendor remain included in planet value.

Reference: Planetarion Fleets and Production.

CHAPTER 15 / 30ALL CHAPTERS ↑

Combat, targeting & defence

Battle calculator

Attack, defence and related fleet operations use the practice combat resolver. Ship class targeting, initiative, damage and armour determine how engagements unfold. Cloaked units and specialised roles may affect what reports show.

Planet protection blocks ordinary attacks until the protection period ends. Hostile alliance structure planets require a declared war with their owner before they can be attacked.

Base fleet behaviour can be set to Stay Home and Fight or Run and Hide. Alliance defence calls identify a planet, hostile ETA and notes; select a ready fleet to respond.

Battle calculator

Under Alliance, paste ship reports into the attacker or defender side, parse their counts and calculate. The result shows starting fleets, losses and survivors. You can also copy counts and results. A calculator result is a practice estimate rather than a guarantee of a live game's outcome.

Covert operations

Military commandResearch and launch checksScope and ratesBonuses

Military command

Open Military → Covert ops to train or dismiss agents and guards, select a practice target, choose an unlocked operation and send agents. Results are instantaneous and appear in the blue Covert ops news category.

Research and launch checks

The existing covert research branch unlocks nine operations. Protection, paused ticks, closed targets, insufficient agents, insufficient resources and exhausted stealth prevent launch. Mission cost is 500 of each resource per agent, also on failure.

Scope and rates

Target changes affect this browser’s practice snapshot; this is not a server-authoritative multiplayer attack system. Training and wages are explicitly shown as Starfall practice rates. Mission rules are based on the Planetarion covert manual.

Bonuses

Quests → Bonuses shows current unused resources, asteroids, RP and CU. The startup grant is imported once: 2,000,000 per resource plus 7,000 CU and 8,000 RP adjusted for race. Historical loyalty defaults to zero because previous-round history is unavailable. Startup rules.

CHAPTER 17 / 30ALL CHAPTERS ↑

Alliance attack tool & fleet worksheet

Claims and permissions

Claims and permissions

Alliance → Attack tool coordinates private operations. Owner, HC and Officer can add or close targets by default; claim permission defaults to all ranks except Recruit. These permissions can be configured in Ranks. One player can hold only one active claim, and each target has only one claimant. Administrators obey the same rules. Only the claimant can release their claim; closing an operation releases its active claim. Round resets clear operations.

Battle calculator offers a compact worksheet: each ship occupies one row with Attacker and Defender count cells. Ship class colours match the legend. Use Tab or arrow keys to navigate. Paste tab-separated numeric columns from a spreadsheet starting at a selected cell: the first column maps to Attacker and the second to Defender. Values must be whole numbers from 0 to 1,000,000,000. Fighters are cyan, Corvettes green, Frigates yellow, Destroyers orange, Cruisers purple and Battleships pink. Reports are simulated and remain on the calculator page.

Waves & scan types

A Wave Amplifier is required to scan. The first amplifier enables scanning; each additional amplifier reduces costs by 0.3%, capped at a 75% discount. Each listed base cost is paid in each of Metal, Crystal and Eonium.

Use the X:Y:Z fields, or enter compact Galaxy:slot coordinates. 2:7 selects galaxy 2, planet slot 7 in your home sector; 07:04:02 is the full form. Paste one coordinate into the paste box, apply it, then choose a scan type to launch.

ScanScan research levelBase cost eachInformation
Planet Scan01,000Planet value, resources, asteroids, guards and production mix.
Landing Scan12,000ETA 1 fleets attacking or defending the target.
Development Scan23,000Construction and planet development status.

Incoming Scan56,000Fleet composition travelling toward your planet.

Landing Scans require a fleet at ETA 1. Incoming Scans require an inbound enemy fleet. The scan cards show the research needed, current cost and whether the action is available.

The appointed scanner, an Alliance Scanner or the Alliance HC can use the available funding controls. Galaxy sweeps require the appropriate scanner or Minister of War permission and enough funding for every target. These permissions remain separate from the option to share reports with everyone.

CHAPTER 19 / 30ALL CHAPTERS ↑

Satelite Uplink & shared intelligence

Store privately or share with all playersSearch and type filtersScans for one planetAnonymous reports

Archive → the Miday array is the central scan archive. Every report has an icon identifying its scan type, target, tick and saved time. Reports remain available for two weeks.

Store privately or share with all players

  1. Open Planet Settings.
  2. Under Quick Actions, find Enable sharing of scans to all people.
  3. Enable it to make your centrally stored scans visible to other game visitors.
  4. Disable it to hide your scans from the shared archive. The central copies remain private.

Sharing starts disabled. Your sign-in identifies the owner of your reports; another player cannot overwrite or delete them. Deleting a saved scan also removes its central copy.

Search and type filters

Search by planet name, coordinates, scan name or words from the report. Each scantype checkbox can be switched on or off, just like news categories. All scan types enables or disables the complete set. Use Refresh Scans for the latest records and Load More Scans when more results are available.

Scans for one planet

The archive button next to P, D, A and U in Galaxy Browser opens all shared scans for that planet, with all types selected. Clear Planet Filter returns to the wider archive.

Anonymous reports

An anonymous report hides its coordinate field and coordinate strings in the shared report text. Anonymous scans are excluded from coordinate-based planet lookups. Their type and target name remain visible.

Everyone means everyone who can access this Site and sign into the game. The site's existing access policy is not changed by scan sharing.

← Waves & scan typesGalaxies, slots & self exile →
CHAPTER 20 / 30ALL CHAPTERS ↑

Galaxies, slots & self exile

Exile Option

Galaxy Browser accepts X:Y coordinates and shows tracked practice planets or deterministic simulated galaxies. Every galaxy displays exactly 15 slots: 1–10 are planet slots and 11–15 are reserved for alliance stronghold structures.

Empty structure slots display Empty / Reserved, even where no stronghold exists. Structure rows have their own labels, and an occupied planet slot is never used for a stronghold structure.

Exile Option

Planet Settings replaces Layout Module with Exile Option. Yes is unchecked by default. Checking it shows confirmation and the exact resource charge before your planet moves to a free slot in a different galaxy. All fleets must be home and you must be able to pay.

The charge is shown separately for each resource. It rises with your previous self-exile count and your galaxy's counted score relative to the average. Free planets pay twice the paid-planet cost. This game uses tracked local galaxy scores to apply the Planetarion self-exile formula.

Payment goes into the galaxy fund of the galaxy you leave. Your fleet, buildings, research and alliance membership remain. The practice relocation is immediate, rather than waiting for one of the next four ticks as in Planetarion.

Counted score records progress gained in the current galaxy. Score brought in through exile does not count as newly earned galaxy score.

CHAPTER 21 / 30ALL CHAPTERS ↑

Politics & galaxy governance

Galaxy politics handles commander votes, minister appointments, a message and banner, trust policies, fund permissions and exile votes. Minister roles cover Communication, Development, War, Economics and scanning.

Galaxy exile votes are different from voluntary self exile. They require funding and minister approvals, and the practice system limits them to two in a 200-tick window. Review the target, reason and displayed cost before opening a vote.

Voluntary self exile moves you into another galaxy and resets the local political context and galaxy-fund view to your new location. Alliance membership is preserved.

Alliances, funds & strongholds

Create or recover an allianceAlliance IntelRanks and permissionsFunds and taxesFortress benefits

Alliance pages cover members, recruitment, defence calls, the battle calculator, alliance funds, fortress placement, structures, relations and logs. Owner and HC manage fortress placement, roles and structures according to rank permissions.

Accepted applicants begin as Recruits. Members can hold Member, Scanner or Officer roles; Owner is the highest rank; Owner changes are restricted to Owners and authorised staff. The alliance supports up to 40 members.

Create or recover an alliance

Open Alliance and enter a unique name, tag, description, recruitment message and MOTD. The creator becomes Owner and receives a personal encrypted passkey. No practice planets are automatically created in the player-only round.

When you have no alliance, the Restore an alliance box remains visible even while ticks are running. Enter your personal Owner passkey to recover a reserved alliance name and its saved attributes. Joining or restoring an alliance hides the box. Recovery does not restore funds, structures, scans or intel.

User control panel → Alliance manager supports five inactive reservations and up to two additional keyholders. Only an Owner or authorised staff can grant or remove Owner rank.

Alliance Intel

Alliance Intel has a separate galaxy browser with its own coordinates, 15 slots, planet and note search, and a dossier for every populated slot. Assess planets as Friendly, Watch or Hostile and save a note. Reports combine your own saved scans with centrally shared reports for those coordinates. Notes and assessments are saved with this device’s practice alliance. Ranks controls who may view intel and edit assessments.

Ranks and permissions

The Ranks tab controls every alliance option for HC, Officer, Scanner, Member and Recruit. By default Members may exchange fund reserves, while only HC can configure minimum reserves and permissions. Each fund exchange must leave all three resulting reserves at or above their configured minimum. The player or game admin with permission access can save a custom role matrix or restore defaults.

Funds and taxes

Donate to Alliance Fund deducts a positive whole amount from your planet and schedules it to arrive after 8 ticks. Combined donations of each resource are capped at two ticks of income per 24 hours. Exchange Resources converts personal reserves, or alliance reserves according to rank permissions, with a 5% fee rounded up to a whole resource unit. For example, giving 1,000 Metal receives 950 Crystal. The result stays in the selected account.

Alliance tax is configurable from 0% to 5%; a planet can enable or disable its contribution in Planet Settings. Donations are limited and scheduled rather than credited immediately. Galaxy Fund is separate and has its own permissions and donation controls.

Fortress benefits

Only alliance members residing in the stronghold galaxy receive the fortress's 0.25% passive resource bonus and its free Wave Distorter every 24 hours. Moving the fortress after the first tick starts a 24-hour anarchy period, with an alliance-wide 2% income penalty.

A stronghold must be placed in a galaxy that contains alliance members. Its structures occupy only slots 11–15.

Transwarp Hub

Reduces alliance travel time by 1 tick for 12 hours, then self-destructs.

Cost: 30% of calculated daily alliance tax income. Cooldown: 12 ticks.

Dyson Sphere

Raises alliance income by 2% for 8 ticks, then self-destructs.

Cost: 10% of calculated daily alliance tax income. Cooldown: 12 ticks.

Ancient Weapons

Raises alliance ship combat stats by 2% for 4 ticks, then self-destructs.

Cost: 40% of calculated daily alliance tax income. Cooldown: 12 ticks.

Voyager IV

Grants 5 Wave Amplifiers to every alliance member. Repeatable.

Cost: 20% of calculated daily alliance tax income. Repeatable.

Solar Flares

Grants 5 Wave Distorters to every alliance member. Repeatable.

Cost: 20% of calculated daily alliance tax income. Repeatable.

Active structures expire according to their displayed tick or hour duration. The five-amplifier and five-distorter megastructure rewards retain their alliance-wide scope; those differ from the fortress's location-specific daily reward.

Alliance ownership & recovery

Create, reserve or recoverRecovery visibilityOwner keys and passphrasesRank rules

Create, reserve or recover

Creating an alliance makes you Owner. Under User control panel → Alliance manager you can reserve up to five inactive alliances, edit your active alliance and add up to two additional keyholders. Reservations do not activate a round alliance until you choose activation.

Recovery visibility

Without an alliance, Restore an alliance stays available even while the ticker runs. Enter your personal Owner passkey to restore the reserved name and attributes. Once you are an alliance member, the recovery box is hidden. Funds, structures, scans and intel are not restored.

Owner keys and passphrases

Each Owner receives a personal encrypted key. Alliance Settings shows only your own key. An optional disclosure passphrase of 12–128 characters allows staff to reveal that specific key on the Keyholders page. Rotating the key invalidates the old key and disclosure phrase. Owner private feeds require the rights of that Owner in the active alliance.

Rank rules

Only an Owner or authorised staff can grant or remove Owner rank. Operational permissions are configurable in Ranks. Attack claim permissions and the one-active-claim limit apply to administrators too.

Alliance Launch Bay & fleet readiness

Permanent fourth fleetLaunch BayMember readinessOfficer launch ordersRank permissions

Permanent fourth fleet

The fleet system now has Base, three personal fleets and a fourth deployable Alliance Fleet. Transfer ships into that slot or deliver a production order there. Normal mission controls cannot launch it. Only ranks granted Control permanent Alliance Fleet can withdraw, launch or recall its ships.

Launch Bay

Open Alliance → Launch Bay to see your permanent fleet and prepare Attack, Defence or Fake Defence with a delay of 0–12 ticks. Existing protection, targeting and fleet availability checks still apply.

Member readiness

Alliance → Defence and Launch Bay show each member in an individual card. Reported idle fleets list ship names, classes and counts. Fleets travelling or scheduled are excluded. Reports refresh every 30 seconds while a member’s game is open; after five minutes they are marked stale. Missing reports remain unknown.

Officer launch orders

A controller can select a member’s reported fourth fleet and queue a mission. The central database checks membership and rank permissions. The member’s open game receives, validates and executes the order on its next sync; offline games wait until reopened. Revoked permissions invalidate unprocessed orders. A round reset clears reports and queued orders.

Rank permissions

Owner, HC and Officer receive View member idle fleets and Control permanent Alliance Fleet by default. The two permissions are separate checkboxes in Alliance → Ranks. Members, Scanners and Recruits do not receive them by default; rank permissions can explicitly delegate or revoke them.

Forums & support tickets

ForumsSupport ticketsAmbient soundtrackTheme preferencesStaff account auditAlliance creation & keyholdersUser and Staff control panelsStaff workspacesStaff structures & battle labMultihunter fleet analysisMultimedia & Discord

Forums

Alliance → Alliance Forums opens the members-only discussion area. Creating a topic or posting a reply advances the Post in your alliance forum achievement; only your own posts in the current alliance count. Galaxy Forum is limited to planets in your own galaxy and advances the Post in the galaxy forum achievement. Community topics support posts and replies. Alliance topics are visible only to members of that alliance. Private alliance and galaxy discussions are cleared by a round reset; community topics remain.

Support tickets

User Control Panel → Support tickets offers Staff support and Ban appeal. Only the requester and staff can read a ticket. Staff can reply and mark requests Open, In progress or Resolved.

Ambient soundtrack

The portal offers an original cinematic desert-space score with mute and volume controls under User Control Panel → Portal theme settings. Browsers may require a click before playback. Music pauses while a portal video plays. In-game music starts disabled; enable it under Planet Settings → Ambient soundtrack.

Theme preferences

Alternate portal themes on every reload cycles all seven portal themes, including Neutral. A fixed selection disables cycling. User Control Panel → Portal theme settings controls the portal and manual theme. Remember setting saves the choice in this browser; theme changes reload the page. Game theme controls remain under Planet Settings.

Staff account audit

Multihunters → Raw access log shows signed-in request metadata and account IP history. Multi groups accounts sharing an observed IP. Only staff can view this data; records expire after 30 days. Shared networks alone do not establish account ownership. Keyholders can authorise staff disclosure of their alliance key with a personal passphrase; rotating the key clears the previous phrase.

Alliance creation & keyholders

Create alliance accepts name, tag, description, recruitment message and MOTD. The creator becomes Owner and receives an encrypted personal passkey. An optional 12–128 character passphrase enables staff disclosure for that specific Owner key; leave empty to disable disclosure. Alliance Controlcenter → Keyholders lists all alliances, including archived key registrations, independently of the alliance selector. The same account can hold separate keys for different alliances. Revealing a key requires its matching alliance, holder and authorised passphrase. Rotation invalidates the old phrase.

User and Staff control panels

The User control panel has a single submenu for Account profile, Portal theme settings, Alliance manager, Support tickets and Create account. Alliance manager permits five pending reservations, with encrypted personal keys and up to two additional holders. Reservations do not change the current round alliance until explicitly activated. Active alliance holders must already be members and become Owners.

Staff account ranks are Player, Support, Multihunter and Administrator. Support handles tickets; Multihunter handles access and fleet review; Administrators manage accounts and game settings. Staff planet audit is readable by all staff roles and lists recorded field changes. It begins recording with this release and cannot reconstruct past field edits. Game and staff workspaces use separate browser saves.

The player-only round contains account-owned planets; automatically generated practice planets are disabled. Resets preserve this mode and keep the ticker stopped until manually started or scheduled anew. The practice schedule processes while an appropriate page is open.

Staff workspaces

Administration now lives under Portal → Staff control panel. Admin Controlcenter, Alliance Controlcenter, Multihunters and Support tickets have dedicated subpages. Staff can continue playing their own assigned planet. The staff workspace saves separately in this browser and does not automatically advance gameplay ticks. Staff overview has a toggle and link to restore the original ingame Administration view.

Staff structures & battle lab

Alliance Controlcenter → Structures displays five reserved slots and construction progress. Staff generation queues a three-tick build without charging the alliance fund, or immediately activates a timed structure. Satelite Uplink → Simulated battle lab generates local test combat reports, can load the starting fleets into Battle calculator. Test reports are labelled simulated, stay in their test module and do not change real assets or farming evidence. Calculator news reports stay on the calculator page.

Multihunter fleet analysis

Staff can open Administration → Multihunters → Fleet farming analysis and select two planets and a tick range. The report lists both directions, attacks, completed battle reports, asteroid captures, losses and repeated launch intervals. At least four attacks and three profitable low-loss battles recommend staff review. Fewer than three completed attack reports produce Insufficient evidence. Events are authenticated account reports from the practice browser, not authoritative server combat evidence. Collection begins with this release; no historical movements are invented. Round generations are kept separate. The analysis never bans a player or proves collusion.

Multimedia & Discord

The portal contains an interface montage and AI battle concept clips with an original cinematic soundtrack: three 24-second battles and an 80-second montage. Discord chat currently contains YouSMP configuration placeholders until an authorised embed is available.

Staff round tools & Havoc

Havoc control boardDummy alliance members

Round setup configures the local round. Planet tools can unlock every research branch or add one of each construction to your current planet.

Havoc control board

Configure research levels, construction counts, resources, asteroids, base-fleet totals per class and minutes per tick. Apply to all immediately sets those values on every saved practice planet. Smaller tick intervals make the game faster. Class totals are distributed across each race’s ship types; active missions retain their fleets.

Reset to previous restores the state from before the most recent Havoc application, including resources, asteroids, fleets and gamespeed. The backup survives page reloads. It is a single-step undo.

Dummy alliance members

Signed-in game admins can select an unassigned dummy in Alliance → Members and add it to the alliance, or create a new dummy member. High Commander rank alone does not show this admin control. Administration → Planets also offers the alliance selector and Add Dummy Member.

The Vesper Chronicles

When the Starfall collapsed the old jumpgate network, five civilisations found themselves stranded around the Vesper Reach. Terran shipyards rebuilt the trade routes. Cathaar listening posts followed signals through the dust. Xandathrii navigators mapped the silent corridors, while Zikonian foundries and Eitraides archives preserved the tools needed to survive.

The eleven command offices issued a shared charter: restore the mines, protect the colonies, and uncover the last transmission of the Miday beacon. No fleet has yet reached its source. Every commander who rebuilds a world brings the Reach one jump closer.
